about: beenster's own Fab motorbike helmet, worn by the rider in place of Data/Rider/helmet.glb when it's on the PC (Fab models are never committed). Tools/ue_build_level.py looks for it first as a static mesh already in the project (Fab plugin import, outside /Game/Rider and /Game/MetaHumans) whose name has one of 'keywords', then in the launcher's Fab cache (VaultCache/FabLibrary, or TORQUE_FAB_VAULT): 'vault' if set, else the newest folder whose name has a keyword, taking its .glb (or .gltf / .fbx). It imports it to /Game/Fab/RiderHelmet with its own materials and fits it over our helmet by their bounding boxes: turned by 'rotate' (pitch, yaw, roll, degrees, applied first), scaled by 'scale' times the size match, then centred plus 'offset' (cm, in our helmet's frame). Every step is logged ('[Torque] fab helmet: ...') so these can be corrected from the log. A MetaHuman package (.mhpkg, which is how Fab gives MetaHuman wardrobe items) is imported first through the MetaHuman plugin's MetaHumanPackageFactory into /Game/Fab/RiderHelmetPkg; a skeletal helmet is drawn in its rest pose.
note: Racing Helmet (Fab, MetaHuman package oa_racinghelmet.mhpkg): round 133's box was 28.3 x 38.3 x 30.7 cm against ours 31.9 x 30.9 x 28.0. It's front-to-back along Y, as MetaHuman assets face +Y, so it's turned -90 degrees in yaw to face +X like ours. It's kept at its own (real) size (fit_size false), only centred on ours. Any slot left on WorldGridMaterial, an /Engine default or a plugin material takes the kit's helmet paint.
